## Motivation

An active hybrid-model request contains more than a reusable prefix: it also owns Mamba recurrent state, generated tokens/logprobs, and native decoding progress. This draft adds an **opt-in, default-disabled** snapshot path to continue that request in a fresh SGLang process after the source exits, without recomputing its committed history.

The supported contract is deliberately bounded: identical model weights/version, source build, TP size, dtype, page/layer geometry, and the same device pair, using trusted shared local storage. Local pool capacity may differ when the actual request allocations fit. Exact sampling-RNG trajectory equivalence, cross-host/weight recovery, crash-atomicity, HA, Trainer integration, and performance are outside this draft's demonstrated scope.

## Modifications

- Export Attention KV plus Mamba conv/temporal state at a committed native decoding boundary; require every TP rank's immutable payload and manifest before source-slot release.
- Reconstruct a new native request with its token/logprob history, normalized sampling parameters, reasoning/stream progress, and remaining generation budget; validate identity and payload integrity before allocating/importing into fresh slots.
- Separate per-request state geometry from local Mamba pool capacity, preserving strict dtype, layer, version, source-build, and TP checks.
- Include public export/resume/reference/negative clients, a public-input reproduction guide, and focused CPU storage/request contracts. No platform launcher, private model data, prompt, logs, or service endpoints are included.
- Align the CPU tests with `CustomTestCase`; handle empty CPU-only `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` in the test runner's port default without changing nonempty-device behavior.

### Relationship to existing work

- [verl#8273](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8273) preserves **resident vLLM** requests through weight updates. This draft provides **SGLang fresh-process continuation at the same weight version**; it does not claim to complete the whole [verl roadmap item](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8186).
- [verl#8168](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8168) restores serving processes/weights and replays requests to rebuild KV. This draft persists the actual hybrid request state.
- [#41694](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41694) and [#39511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39511) provide related hybrid prefix/checkpoint storage work. Generic hybrid cache storage is not a novelty claim here. Feedback on the active-request API, ownership, and reuse of existing storage abstractions is particularly useful; the duplicate search was bounded, not exhaustive.

## Accuracy Tests

**GPU qualification on the original tested base `ed0b8f433f887995b1ce361b15aaf9f6ca93483f`, before refreshing this draft onto `127808733667e7b5b9be38f9dbb72acc6464bab4`:**

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, the same two A100 80GB GPUs, TP2; sequential source exit then fresh target, not two simultaneous engines.
- Actual source/target Mamba pool capacities were 219 and 281 per rank. New target slots received 32,737,280 bytes per rank in total across Attention and Mamba conv/temporal state, with matching digests and no retained source-process record.
- All **128 token IDs and 128 selected-token logprobs** matched an uninterrupted greedy reference exactly (max difference 0): 10 preserved outputs plus 118 new outputs.
- Both TP ranks reported **53 committed history positions, zero historical positions recomputed, 118 completed native decoding inputs, and zero extend inputs**. These are completed-forward observations, not initial zero counters or cache-hit inference. They do not imply zero prefill across a whole workload.
- Owned source exit, an empty GPU compute inventory before target startup, and owned target cleanup were verified separately from the public clients.

**CPU and rejection evidence:**

- The tested capacity revision passed five targeted Linux tests with full module imports and CUDA uninitialized.
- A prior revision passed 27 Linux CPU tests and four real invalid restore requests (version/layout/source binding/manifest reference): HTTP 200 headers followed by SSE error 400, no outputs/import side effects. Those four HTTP cases were not rerun on this refreshed draft.
- Current-base local checks: all applicable pre-commit hooks passed for the changed files; 14 real filesystem-store component cases passed in an isolated harness (CI imports/base projected out, not a full module run); 10 cases exercised the actual runner-port conditional, including reproducing and fixing empty-device visibility; all 13 changed Python files parsed; the three public CLI help commands exited successfully. Complete current-base Linux imports/CI and GPU validation remain pending. Local full-module collection is blocked by unavailable Triton on macOS; no pass is claimed for it.

The GPU prompt is not distributed. [The reproduction guide](https://github.com/donghyq/sglang/blob/d4477f7ee5b3f984a5c39685152c8966da5006e8/examples/runtime/token_kv_restore_README.md) supplies a public input and parameterized commands; that input is not claimed as the previously measured replay. The public clients never start or stop engines.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_token_kv_snapshot_store.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/managers/test_token_kv_snapshot.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This is a correctness feature; no latency, throughput, GPU-hour savings, or cross-weight equivalence is claimed. Normal serving behavior remains default-disabled, but enabled-path overhead still needs measurement before any performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks
- [ ] Current-base Linux CPU CI and related engine CI
- [ ] Human submitter line-by-line review and test review/execution
- [ ] Maintainer agreement on API/lifecycle and storage overlap
- [ ] Current-base GPU qualification before marking ready for merge
- [x] Public reproduction clients and scope documentation

AI assistance (Codex and GLM-5.3) was used for implementation, tests, and documentation. Human submitter line-by-line review remains pending while this PR is a draft; no human review or test attestation is implied.

@@ -0,0 +1,541 @@
+"""Export a paused hybrid request, then restore it on a different native server.
+
+This is a functional HTTP reproducer, not a training or throughput benchmark.
+Run only against dedicated test servers. It never launches or kills a server.
+The export command intentionally leaves its source paused after releasing the
+request's private slots. Stop that source through its original process owner
+before resuming on a newly started server. Snapshot files must be accessible at
+one identical trusted filesystem path on all participating ranks and servers.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.error import HTTPError
+from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+
+def require(value, message):
+    if not value:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def file_ref(path):
+    path = Path(path)
+    raw = path.read_bytes()
+    return {
+        "path": str(path),
+        "bytes": len(raw),
+        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
+    }
+
+
+def write_json(path, value):
+    path = Path(path)
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    temp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
+    temp.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
+    os.replace(temp, path)
+
+
+class HTTP:
+    def __init__(self, url, out, timeout):
+        self.url, self.out, self.timeout = url.rstrip("/"), Path(out), timeout
+        self.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        self.refs = []
+        self.counter = 0
+
+    def call(self, route, payload=None):
+        request = Request(
+            self.url + route,
+            data=json.dumps(payload, allow_nan=False).encode()
+            if payload is not None
+            else None,
+            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        )
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        try:
+            with urlopen(request, timeout=self.timeout) as response:
+                raw = response.read()
+                status = response.status
+        except HTTPError as error:
+            raw, status = error.read(), error.code
+        self.counter += 1
+        path = (
+            self.out
+            / f"http-{self.counter:04d}-{route.strip('/').replace('/', '-')}.json"
+        )
+        record = {
+            "route": route,
+            "payload": payload,
+            "status": status,
+            "elapsed_s": time.perf_counter() - started,
+            "body": raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
+        }
+        write_json(path, record)
+        self.refs.append(file_ref(path))
+        if status < 200 or status >= 300:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{route}: HTTP {status}; immutable response: {path}")
+        value = json.loads(raw)
+        if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("error"):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{route}: engine error; immutable response: {path}")
+        return value, record["elapsed_s"]
+
+
+def token_output(row):
+    meta = row.get("meta_info", {})
+    pairs = meta.get("output_token_logprobs")
+    if not isinstance(pairs, list):
+        raise ValueError("Actual SGLang token IDs and behavior logprobs are missing")
+    ids, probs = [], []
+    for entry in pairs:
+        if not isinstance(entry, (list, tuple)) or len(entry) < 2:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid native output_token_logprobs entry")
+        prob, token = entry[:2]
+        if (
+            type(token) is not int
+            or token < 0
+            or type(prob) not in (int, float)
+            or not math.isfinite(prob)
+            or prob > 1e-5
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Native token/logprob entry is not finite and valid")
+        ids.append(token)
+        probs.append(prob)
+    reason = meta.get("finish_reason")
+    if isinstance(reason, dict):
+        reason = reason.get("type")
+    spans = meta.get("weight_versions", meta.get("weight_version_spans"))
+    version = meta.get("weight_version")
+    if spans is not None:
+        if not isinstance(spans, list) or not spans:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid native weight version spans")
+        cursor = 0
+        versions = set()
+        for span in spans:
+            if (
+                not isinstance(span, dict)
+                or type(span.get("start")) is not int
+                or type(span.get("end")) is not int
+                or span["start"] != cursor
+                or span["end"] < cursor
+                or span["end"] > len(ids)
+                or span.get("version") is None
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "Native version spans do not cover actual generated tokens"
+                )
+            cursor = span["end"]
+            versions.add(span["version"])
+        if cursor != len(ids) or len(versions) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Attempt contains mixed or incompletely observed model versions"
+            )
+        observed = next(iter(versions))
+        if version is not None and observed != version:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Scalar version disagrees with original native version spans"
+            )
+        version = observed
+    return {
+        "token_ids": ids,
+        "logprobs": probs,
+        "stop_reason": reason,
+        "weight_version": version,
+        "raw_meta": meta,
+    }
+
+
+class SSE:
+    def __init__(self, http, payload, stem):
+        self.http, self.payload = http, payload
+        self.path = http.out / (stem + ".jsonl")
+        self.condition = threading.Condition()
+        self.events, self.error, self.done = [], None, False
+        self.start_s = time.perf_counter()
+        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._read, daemon=True)
+        self.thread.start()
+
+    def _read(self):
+        request = Request(
+            self.http.url + "/generate",
+            data=json.dumps(self.payload).encode(),
+            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        )
+        try:
+            with (
+                urlopen(request, timeout=self.http.timeout) as response,
+                self.path.open("w") as out,
+            ):
+                for line in response:
+                    if not line.startswith(b"data:"):
+                        continue
+                    data = line[5:].strip()
+                    if data == b"[DONE]":
+                        continue
+                    row = json.loads(data)
+                    if row.get("error"):
+                        raise RuntimeError("SGLang stream returned an engine error")
+                    event = {"monotonic_s": time.perf_counter(), "raw": row}
+                    out.write(json.dumps(event, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
+                    out.flush()
+                    with self.condition:
+                        self.events.append(event)
+                        self.condition.notify_all()
+        except HTTPError as error:
+            body = error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+            write_json(
+                self.path.with_suffix(".error.json"),
+                {"status": error.code, "body": body},
+            )
+            self.error = RuntimeError(f"generate HTTP {error.code}: {body}")
+        except BaseException as error:
+            self.error = error
+        finally:
+            with self.condition:
+                self.done = True
+                self.condition.notify_all()
+
+    def wait_tokens(self, count, after=None):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.http.timeout
+        with self.condition:
+            while True:
+                for event in self.events:
+                    if after is not None and event["monotonic_s"] <= after:
+                        continue
+                    actual = event["raw"].get("meta_info", {}).get("completion_tokens")
+                    if type(actual) is int and actual >= count:
+                        return event
+                if self.done:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Actual request ended before token {count}"
+                    ) from self.error
+                left = deadline - time.monotonic()
+                if left <= 0:
+                    raise TimeoutError(f"No actual SSE token {count}")
+                self.condition.wait(min(left, 1))
+
+    def finish(self):
+        self.thread.join(self.http.timeout)
+        if self.thread.is_alive():
+            raise TimeoutError("Actual SGLang generation did not finish")
+        if self.error:
+            raise RuntimeError("Actual SGLang generation failed") from self.error
+        if not self.events:
+            raise ValueError("No SGLang generation output")
+        self.http.refs.append(file_ref(self.path))
+        return self.events[-1]
+
+
+def identity_from_inspect(value):
+    identity = value.get("identity")
+    if not isinstance(identity, dict):
+        raise ValueError("Snapshot inspect did not return engine-generated identity")
+    if not identity.get("model_path") or not identity.get(
+        "actual_model_config_file_sha256"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Snapshot identity has no actual model_path/config SHA")
+    if identity.get("weight_version") is None:
+        raise ValueError("Actual engine weight_version is missing")
+    return identity
+
+
+def source_prefix(ack):
+    ids = ack.get("output_ids")
+    probs = ack.get("output_logprobs")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(ids, list)
+        or not isinstance(probs, list)
+        or len(ids) != len(probs)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Snapshot ACK has no actual generated token/logprob checkpoint"
+        )
+    return {"token_ids": ids, "logprobs": probs}
+
+
+def rank_rows(value, tp_size):
+    rows = value.get("ranks", [])
+    require(len(rows) == tp_size, "Missing TP rank responses")
+    by_rank = {row.get("tp_rank"): row for row in rows}
+    require(set(by_rank) == set(range(tp_size)), "Duplicate or foreign TP rank")
+    require(
+        all(row.get("status") == "PASS" for row in rows),
+        "A native rank rejected the operation",
+    )
+    return by_rank
+
+
+def inspect_engine(http):
+    value, _ = http.call("/token_kv_snapshot", {"operation": "inspect"})
+    require(value.get("status") == "PASS", "Unsupported engine")
+    identity = identity_from_inspect(value)
+    require(
+        type(identity.get("tp_size")) is int and identity["tp_size"] > 0,
+        "Missing native TP size",
+    )
+    rank_rows(value, identity["tp_size"])
+    return value, identity
+
+
+def checked_manifest(reference):
+    require(isinstance(reference, dict), "Missing committed manifest reference")
+    observed = file_ref(reference["path"])
+    require(observed == reference, "Committed manifest bytes/SHA differ")
+    return json.loads(Path(reference["path"]).read_text())
+
+
+def export_source(args):
+    http = HTTP(args.engine_url, args.out, args.timeout)
+    initial, identity = inspect_engine(http)
+    rid, snapshot_id = "source_" + uuid4().hex, "snapshot_" + uuid4().hex
+    prompt = args.prompt_file.read_text() if args.prompt_file else args.prompt
+    stream = SSE(
+        http,
+        {
+            "rid": rid,
+            "text": prompt,
+            "stream": True,
+            "return_logprob": True,
+            "logprob_start_len": -1,
+            "sampling_params": {
+                "temperature": args.temperature,
+                "max_new_tokens": args.max_new_tokens,
+            },
+        },
+        "source-generation",
+    )
+    stream.wait_tokens(args.interrupt_at)
+    require(not stream.done, "Source finished before interruption")
+    http.call("/pause_generation", {"mode": "in_place"})
+    guard = {
+        "identity": identity,
+        "expected_weight_version": identity["weight_version"],
+        "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
+        "storage_dir": str(args.storage_dir),
+        "target_rid": rid,
+    }
+    exported, _ = http.call("/token_kv_snapshot", {**guard, "operation": "export"})
+    require(
+        exported.get("snapshot_committed") is True,
+        "All TP ranks must be committed before release",
+    )
+    checked_manifest(exported.get("manifest_ref"))
+    for row in rank_rows(exported, identity["tp_size"]).values():
+        require(
+            set(row.get("state_kinds", []))
+            == {"attention_kv", "mamba_conv", "mamba_temporal"},
+            "Incomplete hybrid state",
+        )
+    prefix = source_prefix(exported)
+    require(
+        len(prefix["token_ids"]) >= args.interrupt_at,
+        "Export has no interrupted token history",
+    )
+    released, _ = http.call(
+        "/token_kv_snapshot",
+        {**guard, "operation": "release", "release_full_gpu_pool": False},
+    )
+    for row in rank_rows(released, identity["tp_size"]).values():
+        require(
+            row.get("old_slots_released") is True and row.get("detached") is True,
+            "Source request still owns native slots",
+        )
+    result = {
+        "status": "CHECKPOINT_READY_SOURCE_LEFT_PAUSED",
+        "identity": identity,
+        "source_rid": rid,
+        "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
+        "storage_dir": str(args.storage_dir),
+        "manifest_ref": exported["manifest_ref"],
+        "source_binding": exported.get("source_binding"),
+        "source_inspect": initial,
+        "export": exported,
+        "release": released,
+        "prefix": prefix,
+        "max_new_tokens": args.max_new_tokens,
+        "whole_gpu_returned": False,

+# Resume an active hybrid request in a fresh process
+
+This opt-in example preserves an active request's Attention KV, Mamba conv and
+temporal state, generated token IDs, selected-token logprobs, and stream progress.
+The target imports the committed state into newly allocated native slots instead
+of prefilling the saved history again.
+
+## Supported scope
+
+Use identical model weights, weight version, source build, TP size, dtype, page
+size, and layer geometry. The GPU qualification used Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP2, on the
+same two A100 80GB devices, sequentially. The target may have a different local
+cache capacity; the request's state geometry must remain compatible and its
+allocations must fit. All TP ranks must have committed payloads before release.
+
+Snapshot files and the HTTP control endpoint must be trusted. The snapshot
+path must be visible at the same absolute path to both engines. This is not
+cross-host recovery, weight-switch preservation, crash-atomic storage, or an HA
+service. Sampling parameters and token history are retained; exact sampled-RNG
+trajectory equivalence is not established. The measured reference uses greedy
+generation. Do not edit a snapshot's identity to bypass a rejection.
+
+## Prepare a public input
+
+From the patched checkout, install SGLang's declared dependencies. Set MODEL to
+a local model path or an available public model identifier. This sample input
+is public and is not the private prompt used for the recorded GPU qualification.
+
+```bash
+export MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
+export RESULT="$PWD/token-kv-example-result"
+export SHARED_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$RESULT/snapshots"
+export PROMPT="$RESULT/prompt.txt"
+export SOURCE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000
+export TARGET_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000
+mkdir -p "$SHARED_SNAPSHOT_DIR"
+cat > "$PROMPT" <<'PROMPT_EOF'
+Explain how plants convert sunlight into chemical energy. Describe the main
+stages in detail, including what happens in the light-dependent reactions and
+the Calvin cycle. Write a connected explanation of approximately 300 words.
+PROMPT_EOF
+```
+
+## Source: reference, committed export, then exit
+
+Start the source in its own terminal. The GPU pair must be available to this
+example. Preserve radix caching and overlap; do not enable speculative decoding,
+PD, PP, CP, DP, ReplaySSM, or additional unsupported side-state pools.
+
+```bash
+SGLANG_ENABLE_TOKEN_KV_SNAPSHOT=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
+  python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.60 --weight-version snapshot-example-v1 --port 30000
+```
+
+After the engine is ready, run the public clients in another terminal:
+
+```bash
+python examples/runtime/token_kv_restore_reference.py capture \
+  --public-helper examples/runtime/token_kv_restore.py \
+  --engine-url "$SOURCE_URL" --prompt-file "$PROMPT" --max-new-tokens 128 \
+  --out "$RESULT/reference" --timeout 300
+python examples/runtime/token_kv_restore.py export \
+  --engine-url "$SOURCE_URL" --prompt-file "$PROMPT" \
+  --storage-dir "$SHARED_SNAPSHOT_DIR" --interrupt-at 8 --max-new-tokens 128 \
+  --temperature 0 --out "$RESULT/source" --timeout 300
+```
+
+Require all TP ranks COMMITTED, retained output history, and successful source
+private-slot release receipts. The CLI leaves the source paused; it does not
+start or stop engines. Stop only this owned source using its own terminal or
+process supervisor, and verify its GPU processes have exited before starting
+the target. Slot release alone is not proof that an entire GPU is free.
+
+## Target: new process, resume, compare
+
+Start a fresh target on the same devices and build. Keep every compatibility
+setting unchanged except the local memory fraction:
+
+```bash
+SGLANG_ENABLE_TOKEN_KV_SNAPSHOT=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
+  python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.65 --weight-version snapshot-example-v1 --port 30000
+```
+
+Once the new engine is ready:
+
+```bash
+python examples/runtime/token_kv_restore.py resume \
+  --source-receipt "$RESULT/source/source-checkpoint.json" \
+  --engine-url "$TARGET_URL" --out "$RESULT/target" --timeout 300
+python examples/runtime/token_kv_restore_reference.py compare \
+  --public-helper examples/runtime/token_kv_restore.py \
+  --reference "$RESULT/reference/reference.json" \
+  --source-receipt "$RESULT/source/source-checkpoint.json" \
+  --restore-result "$RESULT/target/restore-result.json" --out "$RESULT/comparison"
+```
+
+Inspect `correctness.json`, the restore result, and both ranks' completed-forward
+observations. Require exact token IDs and logprobs, complete TP coverage, actual
+new allocations, matching state digests, and zero recomputation of committed
+history. Missing observations are unknown, not zero. Compare each rank's actual
+local capacity rather than inferring capacity from the requested flags. Do not
+sum replicated TP history counts or claim the whole workload had no prefill.
+Stop the owned target after checking results.
+
+## CPU checks
+
+The two registered test files exercise immutable storage, incomplete/corrupt
+records, compatibility rejection, native request reconstruction, batch updates,
+and completed-forward accounting without loading a model:
+
+```bash
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' PYTHONPATH=python   python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_token_kv_snapshot_store.py
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' PYTHONPATH=python   python test/registered/unit/managers/test_token_kv_snapshot.py
+```

+installation without Triton cannot run those complete import paths. Historical
+GPU validation is tied to its recorded source revision; these parameterized
+commands and the public input have not been independently GPU-qualified on the
+refreshed PR base.

+def _descriptor(receipt: dict) -> dict:
+    identity = copy.deepcopy(receipt["identity"])

+        "storage_dir": receipt["storage_dir"],

+def _read_body(response, deadline: float) -> bytes:
+    chunks, size = [], 0
+    while size < 65537:
+        if response.isclosed():
+            break
+        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+        if remaining <= 0:
+            raise TimeoutError("negative response deadline reached")

+            sock = getattr(getattr(owner, "raw", None), "_sock", None)

+    engine_url: str, payload: dict, timeout: float

+    for field in msgspec.structs.fields(params):
+        value = getattr(params, field.name)

+            value = {key: item for key, item in value.items() if key != "__req__"}
+        if isinstance(value, set):
+            value = sorted(value)
+        result[field.name] = value
+    # Refuse CPU callbacks or other objects that cannot survive engine exit.
+    return json.loads(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False))

+    if not inputs or not outputs or any(type(t) is not int for t in inputs + outputs):
+        raise ValueError("Snapshot token history is invalid")
+    if _json_digest(inputs) != metadata["origin_input_ids_sha256"]:
+        raise ValueError("Snapshot original input digest differs")

+        raise ValueError("Snapshot computed prefix is not aligned")

+        raise ValueError("Snapshot pending decode token is not aligned")
+    params = sampling_params_from_snapshot(metadata["resolved_sampling_params"])

+        raise ValueError("Portable restore does not support watermark state")

+def _tensor_inventory(value, prefix=""):
+    result = []
+    if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+        tensor = value.detach().cpu().contiguous()
+        raw = tensor.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).numpy().tobytes()
+        result.append(
+            {
+                "name": prefix,
+                "shape": list(tensor.shape),
+                "dtype": str(tensor.dtype),
+                "bytes": len(raw),
+                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
+            }
+        )
+    elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        for index, item in enumerate(value):
+            result.extend(_tensor_inventory(item, f"{prefix}.{index}"))
+    elif isinstance(value, dict):
+        for key in sorted(value):
+            result.extend(_tensor_inventory(value[key], f"{prefix}.{key}"))
+    elif value is not None:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported tensor payload at {prefix}: {type(value)}")
+    return result

+def _state_receipt(payload):
+    inventory = _tensor_inventory(payload)
+    layout = [{k: v for k, v in item.items() if k != "sha256"} for item in inventory]
+    return {
+        "state_kinds": ["attention_kv", "mamba_conv", "mamba_temporal"],
+        "state_inventory": inventory,
+        "state_inventory_sha256": _json_digest(layout),
+        "state_sha256": _json_digest(inventory),
+        "state_bytes": sum(item["bytes"] for item in inventory),
+    }

+    def _drain_overlap_results(self):
+        """Finish the native overlap result boundary before reading request state.

+        ``pause_generation(in_place)`` intentionally leaves the scheduler state
+        untouched. In overlap mode that can leave one completed forward in
+        ``result_queue``. Processing that result here reuses the scheduler's
+        normal synchronization and request-update path; it does not disable
+        overlap or launch another forward.
+        """
+        scheduler = self.scheduler
+        if not scheduler.enable_overlap:
+            return 0
+        result_queue = getattr(scheduler, "result_queue", None)
+        if result_queue is None:
+            return 0
+        drained = 0
+        while result_queue:
+            batch, result = result_queue.popleft()
+            scheduler.process_batch_result(batch, result)
+            drained += 1
+        # ``last_batch`` is the native overlap marker for a queued result. Once
+        # the queue is fully processed here, keep the scheduler's next iteration
+        # from treating a stale marker as another outstanding result.
+        scheduler.last_batch = None
+        return drained

+    def _read(self, request, identity, store, record):

+    def _release(self, request, identity, store, record):

+            raise ValueError("Request slots were already released")

+            self._request_metadata(req, computed, record["metadata"]["source_binding"])

+                "Source allocator row/slot generation changed after export"

+            bool(other_active_rids)

+            or scheduler.chunked_req is not None

+        if request.release_full_gpu_pool and has_other_work:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Full GPU pool release requires no other active or pending requests"

+        before_free = allocator.available_size()
+        before_rows = self.scheduler.req_to_token_pool.available_size()

+            index for index, item in enumerate(batch.reqs) if item is not req
+        ]

+        record["detached"] = True
+        record["batch_index"] = None

+        # the waiting queue and shared radix prefixes remain native state.

+            self.scheduler.weight_updater.release_memory_occupation(
+                ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=["kv_cache"])
+            )

+        memory_delta = (
+            memory_after["free_bytes"] - memory_before["free_bytes"]
+            if memory_before is not None and memory_after is not None
+            else None
+        )

+            record["memory_suspended"] and memory_delta is not None and memory_delta > 0
+        )

+            **record["state"],
+            **record["metadata"],
+            "source_slots": record["slots"],
+            "allocation_epoch": record["slots"]["request_row_generation"],
+            "old_slots_released": req.kv.req_pool_idx is None

+            "native_release_mode": "release_kv_cache(checkpoint=False)",
+            "shared_prefix_len": shared_prefix_len,
+            "other_active_request_ids": other_active_rids,
+            "allocator_free_tokens_before": before_free,
+            "allocator_free_tokens_after": allocator.available_size(),
+            "request_rows_free_before": before_rows,
+            "request_rows_free_after": self.scheduler.req_to_token_pool.available_size(),
+            "memory_saver_kv_pause_executed": record["memory_suspended"],
+            "full_gpu_pool_released": record["full_gpu_pool_released"],
+            "kv_memory_region_released": record["full_gpu_pool_released"],
+            "weights_memory_region_released": False,
+            "gpu_returned_for_training": False,

+    def _restore(self, request, identity, store, record):

+            raise ValueError("Restore requires released source slots")

+                ResumeMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=["kv_cache"])

+            rows, restored = self._allocate_and_load(
+                req, computed, payload, record["state"]

+                req, rows, computed, record["metadata"]

+            "resumed_decode_input_tokens": 0,
+            "resumed_forward_batches": 0,
+            "resumed_prefill_duration_s": None,

+            "weights_memory_region_released": False,
+            "gpu_returned_for_training": False,

+    def _rank_errors(self, error):
+        errors = [error]
+        if get_parallel().tp_size > 1:
+            errors = [None] * get_parallel().tp_size
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_object(
+                errors, error, group=self.scheduler.tp_cpu_group
+            )
+        failures = [
+            f"rank {rank}: {message}" for rank, message in enumerate(errors) if message
+        ]
+        if failures:
+            raise ValueError("; ".join(failures))

+    def _allocate_and_load(self, req, computed, payload, expected_state):
+        if req.kv.holds_kv or req.kv.holds_mamba:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Portable allocation requires an unowned request resource record"
+            )
+        pool = self.scheduler.req_to_token_pool
+        allocator = self.scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator
+        allocated = (
+            (computed + allocator.page_size - 1) // allocator.page_size
+        ) * allocator.page_size
+        rows = pool.alloc([req])
+        if rows is None:
+            raise ValueError("No free request or GDN rows for portable restore")
+        indices = allocator.alloc(allocated)
+        if indices is None:
+            pool.free_mamba_cache(req)
+            pool.free(req)
+            raise ValueError("No free full-attention KV slots for portable restore")
+        pool.req_to_token[req.kv.req_pool_idx, :computed] = indices[:computed].to(
+            torch.int32
+        )
+        req.kv.kv_committed_len = computed
+        req.kv.kv_allocated_len = computed
+        req.kv.cache_protected_len = 0
+        req.kv.cache_inserted_len = 0
+        req.prefix_len = computed
+        req.refresh_fill_ids()
+        req.extend_end = computed
+        # Every imported token owns a new physical slot. Anchor its native
+        # cache lifecycle at the empty root, so completion can release its
+        # reference and insert the restored sequence into a live radix tree.
+        tree_cache = self.scheduler.tree_cache
+        if not tree_cache.disable:
+            root = tree_cache.root_node_handle(extra_key=req.extra_key)
+            req.last_node = root
+            req.last_host_node = root
+            req.best_match_node = root
+            req.lock = tree_cache.lock(root)

+        req.kv.mamba_needs_clear = False
+        readback = _state_receipt(self._copy(req, computed))
+        if readback != expected_state:
+            raise ValueError("Portable import failed GPU tensor readback verification")
+        return rows, readback

+    def _prepare_portable_decode_batch(self, req, rows, computed, metadata):
+        scheduler = self.scheduler
+        batch = ScheduleBatch.init_new(
+            [req],
+            scheduler.req_to_token_pool,
+            scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator,
+            scheduler.tree_cache,
+            scheduler.model_config,
+            scheduler.enable_overlap,
+            scheduler.spec_algorithm,
+        )
+        batch.forward_mode = ForwardMode.DECODE

+            rows, dtype=torch.int64, device=batch.device
+        )
+        batch.req_pool_indices_cpu = torch.tensor(rows, dtype=torch.int64)
+        batch.seq_lens = torch.tensor(
+            [computed], dtype=torch.int64, device=batch.device
+        )
+        batch.seq_lens_cpu = torch.tensor([computed], dtype=torch.int64)
+        batch.orig_seq_lens = torch.tensor(
+            [computed], dtype=torch.int32, device=batch.device
+        )
+        batch.seq_lens_sum = computed
+        batch.multimodal_inputs = [None]

+        batch.token_ids_logprobs = [req.logprob.token_ids_logprob]

+            batch, scheduler.model_config.vocab_size

+        if penalties.is_required:

+            # only earlier accepted outputs so penalties count each token once.

+                    dtype=torch.int64,

+    def _merge_portable_decode_batch(self, imported):

+            # FutureMap rows before appending the restored request.

+        scheduler.cur_batch_for_debug = running

+    def capture_native_input_intervals(self, batch):
+        """Copy physical-import input positions before this actual native forward."""
+        rows = []
+        for index, req in enumerate(batch.reqs):
+            metrics = self.resume_metrics.get(req.rid, {})
+            prefix = metrics.get("committed_prefix_tokens")
+            if type(prefix) is not int:
+                continue
+            try:
+                if batch.forward_mode.is_extend():
+                    start, end = req.prefix_len, req.extend_end
+                    kind = "extend"
+                elif batch.forward_mode.is_decode():
+                    lengths = batch.seq_lens_cpu
+                    if getattr(lengths, "is_cuda", False):
+                        raise ValueError("counter cannot copy CUDA lengths")
+                    value = lengths[index]
+                    start = int(value.item() if hasattr(value, "item") else value) - 1
+                    end, kind = start + 1, "decode"
+                else:
+                    raise ValueError("unsupported physical input mode")
+                if (
+                    type(start) is not int
+                    or type(end) is not int
+                    or start < 0
+                    or end <= start
+                    or type(batch.forward_iter) is not int
+                ):
+                    raise ValueError("missing native input interval")
+                rows.append(
+                    (
+                        req.rid,
+                        batch.forward_iter,
+                        kind,
+                        start,
+                        end,
+                        prefix,
+                        str(get_serving().weight_version),
+                    )
+                )
+            except Exception:

+                    (
+                        req.rid,
+                        getattr(batch, "forward_iter", None),
+                        "unavailable",
+                        None,
+                        None,
+                        prefix,
+                        None,
+                    )
+                )

+    def observe_native_input_intervals(self, intervals):
+        """Count only intervals carried by this successfully processed result."""
+        for rid, forward, kind, start, end, prefix, version in intervals or ():
+            metrics = self.resume_metrics.get(rid)
+            if metrics is None or "committed_prefix_tokens" not in metrics:
+                continue
+            if metrics["actual_input_counter_status"] == "UNAVAILABLE":
+                continue
+            if (
+                kind == "unavailable"
+                or prefix != metrics["committed_prefix_tokens"]
+                or version != str(get_serving().weight_version)
+            ):
+                metrics["actual_input_counter_status"] = "UNAVAILABLE"
+                metrics["actual_recomputed_tokens"] = None
+                continue
+            if forward in metrics["actual_completed_forward_iters"]:
+                continue
+            metrics["actual_completed_forward_iters"].append(forward)
+            metrics["actual_processed_input_tokens"] += end - start
+            metrics["actual_" + kind + "_input_tokens"] += end - start
+            metrics["actual_recomputed_tokens"] += max(
+                0, min(end, prefix) - max(start, 0)
+            )

+            previous_end = spans[-1]["end"] if spans else 0
+            end = len(req.output_ids)

+"""Atomic, digest-checked files for an opt-in same-version decode checkpoint.
+
+This stores bytes exported by the engine. It does not infer that a token prefix,
+cache hit, or successfully written file constitutes a restored inference state.
+Each TP rank must write its actual tensors before rank zero commits the group.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+
+class TokenKVSnapshotError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _canonical(value: Any) -> bytes:
+    return json.dumps(
+        value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False
+    ).encode("utf-8")
+
+
+def _digest(value: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _fsync_directory(directory: Path) -> None:
+    fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
+    try:
+        os.fsync(fd)
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+def _atomic_write(destination: Path, data: bytes) -> None:
+    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".writing-", dir=destination.parent)
+    try:
+        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
+            handle.write(data)
+            handle.flush()
+            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
+        os.replace(temporary, destination)
+        _fsync_directory(destination.parent)
+    finally:
+        if os.path.exists(temporary):
+            os.unlink(temporary)
+

+class TokenKVSnapshotStore:
+    """Write-once snapshots on a shared filesystem; no pickle is loaded here.
+
+    The scheduler supplies identities from the actual engine, not request labels.
+    A unique snapshot ID is also its storage generation. Repeated writes with the
+    exact same bytes are harmless; conflicting writers and incomplete TP groups
+    are rejected. The engine must deserialize only after ``read_rank`` succeeds.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, root: str | Path):
+        self.root = Path(root).resolve()
+        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    def _directory(self, snapshot_id: str) -> Path:
+        if not isinstance(snapshot_id, str) or not re.fullmatch(
+            r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}", snapshot_id
+        ):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("invalid snapshot ID")
+        directory = self.root / snapshot_id
+        if directory.is_symlink():
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("snapshot directory may not be a symlink")
+        return directory
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_rank(tp_rank: int, tp_size: int) -> None:
+        if (
+            type(tp_rank) is not int
+            or type(tp_size) is not int
+            or tp_size < 1
+            or not 0 <= tp_rank < tp_size
+        ):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("invalid TP rank or world size")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate_identity(identity: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+        if not isinstance(identity, dict) or not identity:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("actual engine identity is required")
+        if "weight_version" not in identity or identity["weight_version"] is None:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("actual engine weight version is required")
+        _canonical(identity)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        try:
+            value = json.loads(path.read_bytes())
+        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError(f"missing or invalid {path.name}") from error
+        if not isinstance(value, dict):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError(f"invalid object in {path.name}")
+        return value
+
+    def write_rank(
+        self,
+        snapshot_id: str,
+        *,
+        tp_rank: int,
+        tp_size: int,
+        identity: dict[str, Any],
+        request_metadata: dict[str, Any],
+        tensor_metadata: dict[str, Any],
+        payload: bytes,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        self._validate_rank(tp_rank, tp_size)
+        self._validate_identity(identity)
+        if not isinstance(payload, bytes) or not payload:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("actual nonempty tensor payload is required")
+        if not isinstance(request_metadata, dict) or not request_metadata:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("request state metadata is required")
+        if not isinstance(tensor_metadata, dict) or not tensor_metadata:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("tensor layout metadata is required")
+        directory = self._directory(snapshot_id)
+        directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+        metadata = {
+            "schema_version": 1,
+            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
+            "tp_rank": tp_rank,
+            "tp_size": tp_size,
+            "identity": identity,
+            "request_metadata": request_metadata,
+            "tensor_metadata": tensor_metadata,
+            "payload_name": f"rank-{tp_rank}.bin",
+            "payload_bytes": len(payload),
+            "payload_sha256": _digest(payload),
+        }
+        metadata_path = directory / f"rank-{tp_rank}.json"
+        # One engine scheduler owns each TP rank. The exclusive lock also rejects
+        # a concurrent/late writer attempting to replace its committed history.
+        lock = directory / f"rank-{tp_rank}.lock"
+        try:
+            fd = os.open(lock, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
+        except FileExistsError as error:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("concurrent rank writer") from error
+        os.close(fd)
+        try:
+            if metadata_path.exists():
+                existing = self._load_json(metadata_path)
+                if _canonical(existing) != _canonical(metadata):
+                    raise TokenKVSnapshotError("conflicting snapshot rank write")
+                self._checked_payload(directory, existing)
+                return existing
+            if (directory / "COMMITTED.json").exists():
+                raise TokenKVSnapshotError("cannot append to committed snapshot")
+            _atomic_write(directory / metadata["payload_name"], payload)
+            _atomic_write(metadata_path, _canonical(metadata))
+            return metadata
+        finally:
+            lock.unlink()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _checked_payload(directory: Path, metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
+        expected_name = f"rank-{metadata['tp_rank']}.bin"
+        if metadata.get("payload_name") != expected_name:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("invalid payload name")
+        path = directory / expected_name
+        if path.is_symlink():
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("payload may not be a symlink")
+        try:
+            payload = path.read_bytes()
+        except OSError as error:
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("missing tensor payload") from error
+        if len(payload) != metadata.get("payload_bytes") or _digest(
+            payload
+        ) != metadata.get("payload_sha256"):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("tensor payload integrity mismatch")
+        return payload
+
+    def commit(self, snapshot_id: str, *, tp_size: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        self._validate_rank(0, tp_size)
+        directory = self._directory(snapshot_id)
+        members = []
+        shared = None
+        for rank in range(tp_size):
+            member = self._load_json(directory / f"rank-{rank}.json")
+            if (
+                member.get("schema_version") != 1
+                or member.get("snapshot_id") != snapshot_id
+                or member.get("tp_rank") != rank
+                or member.get("tp_size") != tp_size
+            ):
+                raise TokenKVSnapshotError("rank layout mismatch")
+            self._validate_identity(member.get("identity"))
+            current = _canonical([member["identity"], member["request_metadata"]])
+            if shared is not None and current != shared:
+                raise TokenKVSnapshotError("TP ranks disagree on model/request state")
+            shared = current
+            self._checked_payload(directory, member)
+            members.append(
+                {"rank": rank, "metadata_sha256": _digest(_canonical(member))}
+            )
+        manifest = {
+            "schema_version": 1,
+            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
+            "tp_size": tp_size,
+            "shared_state_sha256": _digest(shared),
+            "members": members,
+        }
+        committed = directory / "COMMITTED.json"
+        if committed.exists():
+            if _canonical(self._load_json(committed)) != _canonical(manifest):
+                raise TokenKVSnapshotError("conflicting snapshot commit")
+        else:
+            _atomic_write(committed, _canonical(manifest))
+        return manifest
+
+    def read_rank(
+        self,
+        snapshot_id: str,
+        *,
+        tp_rank: int,
+        tp_size: int,
+        expected_identity: dict[str, Any],
+        expected_request_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bytes]:
+        self._validate_rank(tp_rank, tp_size)
+        self._validate_identity(expected_identity)
+        directory = self._directory(snapshot_id)
+        manifest = self._load_json(directory / "COMMITTED.json")
+        if (
+            manifest.get("schema_version") != 1
+            or manifest.get("snapshot_id") != snapshot_id
+            or manifest.get("tp_size") != tp_size
+            or [m.get("rank") for m in manifest.get("members", [])]
+            != list(range(tp_size))
+        ):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("uncommitted or incompatible TP snapshot")
+        metadata = self._load_json(directory / f"rank-{tp_rank}.json")
+        if (
+            metadata.get("schema_version") != 1
+            or metadata.get("snapshot_id") != snapshot_id
+            or metadata.get("tp_rank") != tp_rank
+            or metadata.get("tp_size") != tp_size
+            or _digest(_canonical(metadata))
+            != manifest["members"][tp_rank].get("metadata_sha256")
+        ):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("rank metadata integrity mismatch")
+        if _canonical(metadata["identity"]) != _canonical(expected_identity):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("model/version/cache layout identity mismatch")
+        shared = _canonical([metadata["identity"], metadata["request_metadata"]])
+        if _digest(shared) != manifest.get("shared_state_sha256"):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("request prefix integrity mismatch")
+        if expected_request_metadata is not None and _canonical(
+            metadata["request_metadata"]
+        ) != _canonical(expected_request_metadata):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("request history mismatch")
+        return metadata, self._checked_payload(directory, metadata)
+
+    def receipt(self, snapshot_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Return a reference to the actual commit, rather than an HTTP status."""
+        path = self._directory(snapshot_id) / "COMMITTED.json"
+        manifest = self._load_json(path)
+        if (
+            manifest.get("schema_version") != 1
+            or manifest.get("snapshot_id") != snapshot_id
+        ):
+            raise TokenKVSnapshotError("invalid committed snapshot")
+        raw = path.read_bytes()
+        return {
+            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
+            "snapshot_committed": True,
+            "tp_size": manifest["tp_size"],
+            "manifest_ref": {
+                "path": str(path),
+                "sha256": _digest(raw),
+                "bytes": len(raw),
+            },
+        }
